In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NtAMTs/ NRTs identified in this work are involved in N acquisition and transport in tobacco, and their differential expression patterns suggest their diverse roles in plant growth and N metabolism.

AMT/NRT gene families in plants are composed of a large number of members with diverse expression and regulation patterns in various plant tissues, and that they may play multiple and different roles in plant N acquisition, transport and remobilization, which are likely to be regulated in a complex manner by environmental factors, plant development, and internal N status.

NtAMTs and NRTs have different roles in tobacco, which are respectively associated with NH4+ and/or NO3 acquisition/assimilation, and their expression patterns are regulated by developmental stages, N nutrition, photoperiod and even carbohydrates.
